title: Optimize CPU request path: serialization, thread pool tuning, and thread pinning
author: Priya Singh
description: Motivation: production load tests and flamegraphs showed that a significant portion of end-to-end request CPU on the host was spent outside the GPU-critical path: (1) serialization/parsing and buffer copies for request headers and KV cache lookup; (2) thread-pool contention and frequent wakeups causing syscalls; (3) suboptimal thread placement across NUMA nodes causing cache misses. This PR consolidates a set of targeted CPU-side optimizations to reduce per-request overhead, improve tail latency, and increase throughput under continuous-batching workloads. Changes: 1) Introduced a compact zero-copy request envelope for internal RPCs and runtime request dispatch to avoid frequent memcpy for small headers (redwood/runtime/serialize -> zero_copy_envelope.h/cpp). 2) Reworked the CPU worker thread pool to a per-NUMA pinned worker pool with a lock-free MPMC request queue for hot-path enqueuing. The pool exposes two modes: shared (backwards compatible) and pinned (default disabled). Controlled via env RW_CPU_PINNING and RW_THREADPOOL_WORKER_RATIO. 3) Added a small object arena allocator and request-scoped buffer pool to eliminate thousands of small allocations seen in the profiler. 4) Reduced kernel transitions by batching wakeups: worker threads now use a combined wait-notify with adaptive spin before parking. 5) Optimized KV cache lookup path: avoid redundant reference-counted copies by returning read-only view slices and moving checksum validation off the hot-path where possible. 6) Scheduler change: request routing now considers CPU affinity and current worker utilization to reduce cross-core handoffs for continuous batching. 7) Added new microbench harness and perf-canary job to verify p99 improvements before rollout. Rollout and safety: defaults are backwards-compatible (pinning disabled). Feature gated behind RW_CPU_PINNING and an operator flag in Dedicated. Canary rollout executed in perf-canary fleet for 48h with traffic shadowing before gradual ramp to 25% of host pool. Benchmarks: On our standard language-serving workload (seq_len=512, 8 token generation budget) under 2000 concurrent clients with continuous batching: baseline p99 latency=212ms, new p99=145ms (~31.6% reduction). Throughput (tokens/s) improved from 48k -> 56.6k (~18% uplift) with CPU utilization down ~20% on host. Microbench: zero-copy envelope reduced serialization cycles by ~24%. KV cache path reduced copy-related membandwidth by ~38%. Tests included: unit tests for arena allocator, integration tests for pinned threadpool behavior, end-to-end perf regression tests in perf-canary, and system tests on redwood-private-installer. Impacted files: listed below. Checklist: - [x] Benchmarks added and reproducible scripts included - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Canary run completed - [x] Feature flags and config knobs documented - [x] Rollout plan and rollback steps documented Related: This work addresses ENG-3421 (reduce CPU per-request) and ENG-3470 (KV cache copy elimination) and was prompted by INT-2035 incident analysis. See linked perf artifacts in the internal perf dashboard for raw traces.

review_comments: Luca Romano: High level this looks great; can we make pinning opt-in behind config and document cost tradeoffs? Also please add metrics for cross-core handoffs.
Priya Singh (reply): Pinning is behind RW_CPU_PINNING and default off; added metrics redwood.runtime.thread_handoffs and redwood.runtime.worker_affinity to the PR and the perf dashboard.
Marta Chen: The lock-free queue is clever but let's add a mitigation for the ABA window on 32-bit platforms. Also add a fallback to the old queue if the platform lacks required atomics.
Priya Singh (reply): Added a gated compile-time check and a fallback to the previous MPMC on unsupported targets (see pinned_worker_pool.cpp).
Dylan Park: Observed one flaky test in the CI matrix (allocator unit test) on macOS runners; is that a known allocation order dependence?
Priya Singh (reply): Fixed by enforcing deterministic free-list ordering in the test harness; re-ran CI and test stabilized.
release_notes: Performance: Reduced CPU-side request overhead by optimizing serialization, adding a NUMA-aware pinned thread pool, introducing an arena allocator, and reducing KV cache copies. Expected p99 latency reduction ~30% in standard workloads and throughput uplift ~18%. Feature gated (RW_CPU_PINNING) and rolled out via perf-canary.
notes_for_ops: Defaults are backwards compatible. To enable pinned mode set RW_CPU_PINNING=1 and tune RW_THREADPOOL_WORKER_RATIO to control worker count per socket. Rollback: disable RW_CPU_PINNING and restart runtime. Monitor redwood.runtime.thread_handoffs and redwood.runtime.worker_affinity metrics during ramp.
